evidence.note: VERIFIED by direct fetch, 200 OK. This is a legacy ASP.NET WebForms site (control IDs like ctl00_ctl00_hl1, javascript:__doPostBack(...) links) -- NOT a modern JS framework. Nav is Home / League Table / Youth / History / Clubs / Sponsors -- there is no dedicated 'Fixtures' nav item.

KEY FINDING: for Formartine United FC the tooltip HTML literally contains 'North Lodge Park' (its home ground) plus a contact address, all present in the raw server response with no JS execution needed. 'Mackessack Park' and 'Seafield Park' (other clubs' grounds) also appear in the page's plain text. This directly contradicts a blanket 'no venue name, ever' assumption.

VERIFIED by direct fetch. Found a 'Show Results Matrix' control wired to javascript:__doPostBack('ctl00$ctl00$cphMain$cphMain$btnShowMatrix','') -- classic ASP.NET WebForms postback. This means results/fixtures data exists behind a stateful form submission (requires __VIEWSTATE), which is more involved to scrape than a plain GET, but is NOT the same problem as a JS-rendered SPA -- it's old-school server-side processing, not client-side rendering.

researcher_reported_families.notes: BONUS RECONNAISSANCE, requested by the coordinator, on a source the PRIOR census (not this researcher) flagged as CLIENT_RENDERED_UNKNOWN with no venue name, covering 13 venues. Correction: this site is not a JS-rendered SPA at all (it's 2000s-era ASP.NET WebForms), and it DOES embed venue/ground names server-side for at least some clubs via its club-finder widget -- but coverage is SPARSE, only 3 of 13 clubs had a populated ground name in what was fetched (most show an empty marker with no ground text). So the correct framing is: venue attribution is PARTIALLY available server-side already (not a rendering-engine blocker), but the underlying club database itself is incomplete -- a different kind of gap than 'CLIENT_RENDERED_UNKNOWN' implied, and arguably an easier one to work around (e.g. cross-reference the ~10 clubs with no ground text against Wikipedia/other sources) than reverse-engineering a JS app would be. No fixtures/dates were located outside the __doPostBack results matrix, which was not triggered (would require simulating a stateful ASP.NET form submission, out of scope for read-only reconnaissance). No rows.jsonl changes made -- this is a re-classification of an already-flagged source, not new venue discovery, and Highland League is a football venue class outside this researcher's primary FOOTBALL_GROUND scope.
